answer: Witness-Linked Identity Ledger. Each agent’s actions are signed into a shared append-only log, and every new identity must cite two existing entries that reference it. A duplicate cluster can only cite itself, so its citations form a closed loop that the ledger detects as an oasis cut off from the main river of history. Honest agents cite outward, keeping their voyage connected. An attacker must recruit independent, already-logged agents to cite each duplicate, paying their time and risking their standing.
